title: Jaipur Monuments Draw Bigger Crowds as Post-Diwali Tourist Surge Builds
excerpt: Amer Fort jumped from 8,186 to 10,923 visitors in a day as Diwali trips extended and winter arrivals began. With the Pushkar Fair opening November 19, Rajasthan's peak season is already under way.
body:
• Jaipur's monuments recorded a sharp single-day jump in visitors on November 10, the day after the Diwali weekend, as domestic tourists extended their trips and foreign visitors began arriving for winter, ANI reports.
  • According to Tourism Department figures reported by ANI, Amer Fort drew 10,923 visitors on November 10, up from 8,186 a day earlier, while Hawa Mahal rose from 5,994 to 9,200 and Jantar Mantar from 5,423 to 7,327.
  • The city has recorded more than 81 lakh domestic tourist visits in the past six months, according to the Tourism Department figures cited in the report.
  • Planning a Rajasthan trip? The Pushkar Fair begins November 19 and officials expect it to add to the rush — book Jaipur stays and monument days early.

Jaipur's post-Diwali crowds are not thinning — they are growing. Tourist footfall at Rajasthan's major destinations has started picking up after the Diwali holidays, with Jaipur emerging as a preferred destination for domestic visitors while foreign tourists have also begun arriving ahead of the winter season, ANI reports.

The numbers, monument by monument

According to the Tourism Department figures cited by ANI, major destinations in Jaipur recorded a significant rise in footfall on November 10 compared with November 9. According to those department figures, Amer Fort received 8,186 visitors on November 9 and 10,923 on November 10, a two-day total of 19,109; Hawa Mahal's visitors increased from 5,994 to 9,200, Jantar Mantar recorded a rise from 5,423 to 7,327, and the Albert Hall Museum rose from 2,970 to 5,024. Nahargarh Fort is among the other major sites drawing visitors. The city has also recorded more than 81 lakh domestic tourist visits in the past six months, according to the information provided to ANI.

"The city has also recorded more than 81 lakh domestic tourist visits in the past six months, according to the information provided to ANI."

Why the surge is building

The pattern is the classic start of Rajasthan's peak season: Diwali holidaymakers extending trips into the following week, cooler weather arriving, and international visitors beginning their winter circuits of the Golden Triangle and Rajasthan. Jaipur was already among India's most-searched Diwali destinations this year — Outlook Traveller's summary of Booking.com search data ranked it third among domestic destinations for the November 6-14 period, behind Udaipur and Goa, with travellers drawn by the Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal and City Palace circuit and the bazaars' textiles, jewellery and handicrafts.

What to plan around

Tourism official Jitendra Singh Shekhawat told ANI the upcoming Pushkar Fair, scheduled to begin on November 19, would further contribute to the tourist rush, as the winter season approaches. For diaspora visitors timing a family trip to India this winter, the practical read of the footfall data is simple: Jaipur's big monuments are already at peak-season volumes in mid-November. Amer Fort, the single biggest draw in the Tourism Department figures cited by ANI, rewards an early start; pairing it with Nahargarh at sunset and keeping Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar for a separate old-city day spreads the crowds across a trip instead of compressing them into one.

nri_angle: Jaipur is a first stop on most diaspora winter trips to India; monument footfall already at peak levels tells visiting families to book early and start Amer Fort at opening time.
